points: A famous chapter of nechamah, with many lines we say in davening.
The people say Hashem only loved us long ago, at Yetzias Mitzrayim. Hashem answers: "Ahavas olam ahavtich," an eternal love. That's why we say Ahavas Olam at Maariv, in the dark of night.

Hashem promises to rebuild, especially the northern kingdom, and calls Efraim "my firstborn." Had Rachel not given Leah the signs, Efraim might have been the bechor and the kingdom might never have split.
"Rachel mevakah al baneha": Rachel cries, maybe my good deed caused all this. Hashem answers: "Yesh sachar lif'ulasech," there is reward, and your children will return.
Hashem plays the long game. In the short term a good deed can look like it backfired, but no good deed goes unrewarded.
